summary.text: A 48-year-old premenopausal woman presented with a right breast mass noticed for about 6 weeks; mammography, ultrasound and DCE-MRI showed an irregular mass in the upper outer quadrant.

Core needle biopsy confirmed ER/PR-positive, HER2-negative invasive ductal carcinoma, nuclear grade 3, Ki-67 70%; she had right breast-conserving surgery (pT2N1mi) followed by adriamycin and cyclophosphamide chemotherapy without adjuvant radiation.

Five months after surgery, CT and ultrasound showed a new rim-enhancing, complex cystic and solid lesion near the operation site; biopsy showed invasive carcinoma with squamous differentiation, and complete resection confirmed pure squamous cell carcinoma, triple-negative with Ki-67 60%.
Staging imaging found no primary SCC outside the breast; she received curative radiotherapy, and 17 months after the second resection developed multiple metastases to the right axilla and lungs.

social_exposures.note: No social or exposure history is documented.

care_plans.note: No follow-up or care plan is documented beyond treatments received.

ambiguities.issue: The text states the first IDC was treated with breast-conserving surgery and chemotherapy, then a squamous cell carcinoma was found near the same site five months later; the authors call the tumors synchronous primaries rather than recurrence, but the exact interval between them is only given as five months.

evidence.quote: Herein, we present an unusual case highlighting the synchronous development of primary SCC and IDC in the ipsilateral breast.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer recurrence of IDC or any radiation-induced origin.

ambiguities.issue: The second breast ultrasound sentence ("In addition, breast ultrasound identified ...") follows the chest CT sentence led by "Five months post-operation"; the lead clause belongs to the CT sentence and is not a heading, so the ultrasound time is left null and its order relative to the CT is unknown.

evidence.quote: Five months post-operation, chest computed tomography (CT) showed
In addition, breast ultrasound identified

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign the five-month time to the ultrasound.

ambiguities.issue: The source does not state whether the axillary and lung metastases arose from the IDC or the SCC, so they are recorded as a condition and outcome without a tumor link or metastatic sites on either tumor.

figures.caption_summary:
Fig. (3)
Histopathological findings of the primary pure squamous cell carcinoma of the breast. (A) Low-power view showing the overall architecture of the tumor, with nests and sheets of malignant squamous cells invading the breast parenchyma (hematoxylin-eosin [H&E] stain, original magnification: x40). (B) High-power view highlighting the prominent keratinization (H&E stain, original magnification: x200). (C) p40 immunohistochemistry showing strong nuclear positivity in tumor cells (Original magnification: x200). (D) Estrogen receptor immunohistochemistry showing negativity in the tumor cells (Original magnification: x200).
